Commercial Tools

Every one of the 65 entries in this index is an open-source project — each links to a public repository and declares a licence (7 distinct licences across the set). Vendor and paid products are not listed yet, and upstream does not list them either.

Why the split matters

The risk flags on this site answer one question: what does this do to my machine? For open-source tools that is checkable — the code is right there, and the guide explains how each flag is derived. A commercial product is a different bargain: you are trusting a vendor's description instead of reading the source, so the same flags cannot be verified the same way. Mixing the two in one table would quietly weaken every label on the page.

What a listing would need

A public product page Reachable without a sales call, so the description can be checked
Deployment model Runs on your host, or a hosted service — this changes what the flags mean
What it tests Which of the scopes it covers
Pricing shape At minimum, whether there is a free or trial tier
Independent evidence Docs, a public changelog, or third-party evaluation — something that is not marketing

Suggesting one

Curation happens upstream at aisecuritymatrix.com. Raise the suggestion there; this mirror picks up changes on its next sync. For anything about this mirror itself — translations, layout, a wrong flag — see Contribute.
